title: Gated release decision service with explainable eval provenance
creator: Priya Singh
description: Goal: Implement a centralized decision service that evaluates canary and A/B exposures against curated eval suites and production telemetry, produces human-readable decisions with metric provenance, and triggers automated rollback or progressive ramp actions when policies are violated. This ticket covers the core decision engine, policy templates, provenance capture, and integration endpoints for the rollout controller and Console.
design_summary: 1) Ingest: evaluation pipelines (golden prompt sets, cohort probes) and sampled production telemetry (latency p95, hallucination flags, user satisfaction signals). 2) Normalization & attribution: align metric definitions across model/config variants; tag each metric with provenance (promptset version, model commit hash, quantization profile, runtime flags). 3) Statistical test layer: configurable tests (bootstrap CI, sequential probability ratio test, non-parametric rank tests) with false discovery controls for multiple metrics. 4) Decision rules: policy templates combining thresholds, delta windows, and severity weights producing a Decision object (ALLOW, WARN, BLOCK, ROLLBACK) with confidence score and top contributing signals. 5) Action layer: call rollout-controller API to reduce traffic, stop rollout, or trigger full rollback; emit audit trail and explainable rationale for Console/UI and for audit logs.
metric_set: Primary: answer-quality delta (A/B/Canary vs baseline), hallucination rate, safety filter hit rate, inference latency (p50/p95), token cost delta. Secondary: traffic skew, error rate, QA review failure rate. Each metric captured with sample sizes and cohort identifiers.
gating_logic: Support both instantaneous canary gating (sampled traffic window e.g., 5k requests or 1 hour) and progressive A/B gates (sequential checkpoints at 1%, 10%, 50%). For each checkpoint: run configured statistical tests, compute weighted severity score; if severity exceeds policy threshold then either pause ramp or invoke rollback. Policies may be configured per-customer/project and include 'grace windows', 'escalation steps', and manual approval overrides.
provenance_and_explainability: Every Decision object includes: metric snapshots (baseline, variant), sample counts, test type and p-values/CI, top 3 contributing prompts/cohorts, model/config diff, and linked artifacts (PR, data set version). UI will show a human-readable summary and a collapsible provenance trail for auditors.
integration_points: - Rollout controller REST endpoint (existing controller) for actions. - Console: gating dashboard + provenance viewer + manual override buttons. - Alerting: PagerDuty and Slack channels for high-severity decisions. - Audit logs: append-only store with Decision ID and trace IDs linked to GitHub PR and eval job IDs.
implementation_plan: M1 (2 weeks): Decision API + basic policy interpreter + ingest connector for eval-job outputs. M2 (2 weeks): Statistical test module, provenance enrichment, synthetic regression simulator for tests. M3 (2 weeks): Controller action integration, Console UI hooks, and canary flow in staging. M4 (1 week): Hardening, policy editor, rollouts to internal teams. M5 (1 week): Run safety pilot with selected customers.
testing_and_validation: - Unit tests for policy evaluation and statistical test edge cases. - Integration tests with traffic-simulator to inject controlled regressions (semantic and latency). - Staging run with mirrored production traffic and synthetic regression vectors to validate detection sensitivity and false-positive rate. - Post-deploy 'shadow' mode for 2 weeks to compare decisions against manual ops decisions before enabling automatic actions.
observability: Decision metrics exported: decisions_per_minute, avg_decision_latency, percent_decisions_with_action, false_positive_rate_estimate (from shadow runs). Per-decision traces include links to timeseries for contributing metrics and to the original eval job. Console charting for checkpoint progression and rollback events.
operational_playbook: - Default policy: block rollout if answer-quality delta drops >3% with p<0.01 OR hallucination increase >1% absolute. - On BLOCK: rollback to last stable model and notify SRE/PM on-call. - For WARN decisions: pause ramp and create an incident ticket for triage. - For low-confidence failures, escalate to manual review before action.
security_considerations: Provenance store contains model commit IDs and eval prompt text; ensure encryption at rest and RBAC for access in Console. Audit logs immutable and available to compliance team. Security review required before enabling auto-rollback for customer-visible releases.
open_questions: 1) Which default statistical tests should we enable (bootstrap vs SPRT) for small-sample canaries? 2) How to express multi-metric trade-offs in a concise policy DSL? 3) Allowed delay between decision and controller action for different customer tiers?
acceptance_criteria: - Decision service returns deterministic Decision objects for canonical test vectors. - End-to-end test that triggers automated rollback in staging when synthetic regression is injected. - Console shows provenance and links to eval job/PR. - Shadow-mode run for 14 days with false-positive rate <= 2% on internal traffic.
